sn56.41:1.3: “Speculation about the world” is said to be one of the four trains of thought that can drive you mad ([an4.77:1.9]()). At [mn48:8.9]() it is distinguished as speculation about this world and the next. | The Buddha once visited the Sumāgadhā pond to accept Nigrodha’s challenge. There was a peacock’s feeding ground nearby. The Rāmāyaṇa describes the river Sumāgadhī, which rises among the five hills of Rajagaha like a gorgeous garland (1.31.7); this must be a lake on that river. Perhaps to be identified with the modern Dhadhar.
